intro: Look at how it stretches on and on. This is Uzunköprü Bridge in Edirne province, from 1443. At 1,238 metres over the Ergene, it is the longest stone arch bridge in the world, and the keystones of its 174 arches carry lions, elephants, tulips and other figures.
history: The bridge was completed for Murad II in 1443. It crosses the marshy plain of the Ergene, and it linked Edirne to western Thrace. At 1,238 metres it is the longest stone arch bridge in the world. The town founded at its head took its name from it, and today it is the district centre.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the 174 arches and the keystone reliefs, stop at the fountain at the bridgehead, and look for the flood relief openings.
facts: Did you know? The keystones carry lions, elephants, tulips and eagles, and none is repeated: every arch bears its own mark. And at 1,238 metres, this is the longest stone arch bridge in the world.
outro: This brings our journey across Uzunköprü Bridge to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
